Hi team —

Following up from product marketing, Datasift asked us to publish a short, plain-language privacy blurb that will appear in the Hosted API docs and the Console privacy tooltip. Their legal asked for a quick read for anything that could be misinterpreted around subprocessors and transfers.

I attached the draft (hosted_api_privacy_blurb_v1.docx). High-level asks:
- Can legal confirm the "we may use subprocessors" sentence is accurate and sufficient?
- Product: can the full paragraph be condensed to one 2-line tooltip variant (UI has ~220 chars)?
- Security: do we need an explicit sentence mentioning SCCs, and if so, what's the simplest language?

Emma, looping you in so Datasift can confirm anything that would block them from linking to our public docs.

Thanks — please reply inline where possible.

Subject: Re: Public-facing privacy blurb for Hosted API & Console — plain-language review

Thanks, Sergio. I reviewed the draft and attached a redline (redlined_blurb.docx) with suggested edits. Top-line: the content is generally fine but we should tighten a few phrases so they are not ambiguous for customers. My comments below — please treat as proposed public copy (short + long).

1) Subprocessor language
Current: "We may use subprocessors to process data on our behalf."
Suggested: "We may engage subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, analytics services) to process customer content on behalf of the customer. Our DPA requires subprocessors to follow the same data protection obligations we have with you."
Why: "process data on our behalf" is vague — specify "customer content" to avoid implying we process customers' internal data for other purposes. Also call out that subprocessors are contractually bound.

2) Transfers & safeguards
Short line (tooltip-friendly): "When data moves outside the EU, we use standard contractual clauses and other safeguards required by law."
Long paragraph: "If customer content is transferred across borders we rely on lawful transfer mechanisms such as Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), EU adequacy decisions, or customer-specific contractual safeguards. Customers can request a copy of our DPA and current subprocessor list at the link below."

3) Retention & purpose
Add one sentence: "We keep customer content only as needed to provide the service, comply with the law, or as the customer requests in the DPA."

4) Links & visibility
Please add a clear link to the DPA and to the live subprocessor list (not a PDF snapshot) — avoid statements like "see attached" for public docs.

I left inline comments about tone and an alternative two-line tooltip for the Console UI. Happy to iterate.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park | Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Attachments: redlined_blurb.docx (Word doc, redline)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-10-03T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Public-facing privacy blurb for Hosted API & Console — plain-language review

Thanks Kim — these are great. Quick product note: the Console tooltip space is limited to ~220 characters. I rewrote two options below:

- Tooltip (short): "We process customer-provided content to provide the Hosted API. Transfers outside the EU use SCCs or other legal safeguards. See DPA & subprocessor list for details." (198 chars)

- Expanded help text (for docs): "We process customer content to operate the Hosted API. We may engage subprocessors (for example, cloud providers) who are contractually required to protect your data. When data moves across borders we rely on legal transfer mechanisms such as Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). You can find our DPA and live subprocessor list at the link below."

Product questions:
- Do we want to reference "customer content" in both UI and docs (Kim recommends yes).
- Should we add a one-line privacy contact for EU customers? That would read: "For DPA or transfer questions contact privacy@redwood.ai."

If legal signs off I can slot the short tooltip into next week's Console release and the expanded copy into the Docs site. Emma — would the short tooltip work for Datasift's reference?

—Laura
